propositions.title: Exact score likelihood has a unique finite trait MLE exactly for an interior score
assumptions: J>=1 observed locally independent Rasch items; fixed finite known difficulties b_j
S is an integer in[0,J]; trait theta is an unrestricted finite real parameter
Likelihood conditional on the specified observed mask; no extra theta-dependent missingness factor is silently omitted
proof: The exact score log likelihood is ell(theta)=log c_S(b)+S theta-sum_j softplus(theta-b_j). Coefficient c_S is positive and finite for finite b and is independent of theta.
Let p_j(theta)=logistic(theta-b_j). Then ell prime=S-sum p_j and ell double-prime=-sum p_j(1-p_j)<0 at every finite theta.

As theta tends to minus infinity ell prime tends to S; as theta tends to plus infinity it tends to S-J. For0<S<J, continuity and strict decrease give exactly one finite zero of ell prime, which is the unique global maximum.

ForS=0 the derivative is strictly negative, so no finite maximizer exists and probability tends to1 as theta tends to minus infinity. ForS=J it is strictly positive, with analogous plus-infinity supremum. ForJ=0 the likelihood is constant and every theta maximizes it.
propositions.limit: This is a trait-coordinate likelihood conditional on known calibration. The observed marginal likelihood of biometric hyperparameters is different.

propositions.title: Fixed proper Gaussian trait prior gives a unique conditional trait-block MAP, including empty masks
assumptions: A finite-dimensional trait vector theta has a fixed Gaussian prior N(m,Q^-1) with symmetric positive-definite finite Q
Conditionally independent calibrated Rasch likelihood factors, each with its own known observed-item mask; masks may be empty
All other parameters and random effects determining m,Q are held fixed; any missingness factor must either be theta-independent or separately checked
proof: Its log posterior equals a constant plus sum_i ell_i(theta_i)-0.5(theta-m)^T Q(theta-m).

The Hessian is -Q-diag(sum_j p_ij(1-p_ij)). For any nonzero vector h, h^T Hessian h is strictly negative because Q is positive definite and each added diagonal is nonnegative. Thus the log posterior is strictly concave.

Every exact score probability is at most1, so sum ell_i<=0. The Gaussian quadratic tends to minus infinity as the norm of theta tends to infinity. The continuous log posterior is coercive and attains a finite maximum; strict concavity makes it unique.

ForChapter2 this applies to theta conditional on genetic/common effects and finite hyperparameters: residual variances exp(beta0+beta1*a) are strictly positive. It does not apply to the non-Gaussian marginal theta prior when beta1 is nonzero.

ForChapter5, with fixed moderator and hyperparameters, the Gaussian twin-phenotype prior also has positive-definite covariance when unique-environmental variances are positive; the result applies to that fixed block.
propositions.limit: This is uniqueness of a conditional posterior mode, not unique marginal-likelihood maxima, joint posterior log concavity, unbiasedness, power, a sampler implementation or measured speedup.

propositions.title: Chapter2 centered augmented posterior need not be jointly log-concave under unchanged source priors
setup: Use any design containing at least one MZ pair, known finite Rasch difficulties and J>=1 observed items per twin. This includes the structural source design; the argument is not based on its unavailable empirical observations.

Take finite interior precision ta=1, fix mu=0,beta0=0 and common effects at0. Let the selected shared MZ genetic effect be a, both selected traits equal a, and let v denote the source beta1 slope. Fix all other genetic effects and traits at0. This is an affine slice in independent centered coordinates; deterministic a2=a1 is represented only once.
Hold all other parameters and latent effects fixed at finite valid states. The source slope prior has variance10, hence negative-log prior v^2/20. The genetic effect contributes a^2/2.
proof: Selected conditional theta residuals are zero along the slice. Their two Gaussian normalizing terms sum to v*a. Other zero genetic effects have environmental variances independent of v. Constants and linear observation terms do not affect curvature.
The restricted negative-log posterior is F2(a,v)=a^2/2+v^2/20+v*a+2 sum_j softplus(a-b_j)-S_pair*a+constant.
Its Hessian is [[1+d(a),1],[1,1/10]], where d(a)=2 sum_j p_j(a)(1-p_j(a)). Thus determinant=(1+d)/10-1.

As a tends to plus infinity, d tends to0 for every finite calibration. In particular take a>=max_j b_j+log(4J). Then d<=1/2 and the determinant<=-17/20<0. Both a and all other parameter/latent values are finite.

A concave log posterior would have concave restrictions to every affine slice, but this Hessian is indefinite. Thus the centered augmented posterior is not globally log-concave. This statement holds for any observed response pattern because scores enter only linearly.
propositions.limit: Nonconcavity does not imply multiple local or global modes. It is coordinate-dependent and says nothing by itself about the marginal hyperparameter likelihood or the behavior of the tested sampler.

propositions.title: Chapter5 centered augmented posterior likewise has an explicit nonconcave slice
setup: Use a design with an MZ pair whose shared moderator is1, known finite Rasch difficulties, J>=1 items per twin and the source normal variance10 prior for the genetic moderation slope v=beta1a.

Fix genetic logvariance intercept beta0a=0 and other finite hyperparameters; set mu=main=c=0, selected shared genetic effect a and selected theta1=theta2=a. Set other genetic effects and traits to0. All component variances remain strictly positive.
The selected genetic effect has variance exp(v). Other families with moderator1 and zero genetic effect add only terms linear in v; moderator0 families add no v curvature.
proof: The restricted negative-log posterior is F5(a,v)=a^2 exp(-v)/2+v^2/20+k*v/2+2 sum_j softplus(a-b_j)-S_pair*a+constant, where k is the fixed number of relevant Gaussian genetic density normalizers. Its exact value does not affect the Hessian.
Atv=0 the Hessian is [[1+d(a),-a],[-a,a^2/2+1/10]]. Its determinant is 1/10-a^2/2+d(a)*(a^2/2+1/10).
Choose finite a>=max(1,max_j b_j+log(20J)). Since p(1-p)<=exp(-(a-b_j)), d<=1/10. The determinant is therefore <=11/100-9a^2/20<=-34/100<0.
Hence this source-faithful centered augmented posterior is not globally log-concave, notwithstanding the strictly log-concave conditional trait block.
propositions.exact_fixture: ForJ=60,b=0,a=10,v=0, exp(10)>2^10, so d<120/1024. The exact rational determinant upper bound is -56357/1280<0.
propositions.limit: This does not refute an at-most-one maximum statement for the observed marginal likelihood, nor prove posterior multimodality. It only rules out this particular global joint-concavity route to proving such a statement.

scientific_equivalence_boundaries: Known calibration and correct item masks are essential for the score reduction; inference on item difficulties cannot drop calibration-dependent constants.
A Gaussian sum-score phenotype comparator is not the exact score model.
P2 and the nonconcavity witnesses concern different parameter blocks/objectives; there is no contradiction.
The augmented posterior densities use centered physical latent coordinates. Their concavity is not invariant under nonlinear reparameterization.
The observed-data marginal hyperparameter likelihood is an integral over latent variables. Neither a unique conditional MAP nor a nonconcave joint density settles its number of maxima.
A nonconcave function can have a unique maximum; no multiple-maxima claim is made.
